verses.43:2: Deus, com os nossos ouvidos ouvimos: * os nossos pais nos anunciaram:
verses.43:2b: a obra que {operatus} nos dias deles, * e nos dias antigos.
verses.43:3: A vossa mão exterminou as nações, e vós os plantastes: * afligistes os povos, e os expulsastes.
verses.43:4: Pois não possuíram a terra com a própria espada, * e o braço deles não os salvou:
verses.43:4b: mas a vossa direita, e o vosso braço, e {illuminatio} do vosso rosto: * porque {complacuisti} neles.
verses.43:5: {ipse} meu Rei e meu Deus: * que {mandas}.
verses.43:6: Em vós, com o chifre, {ventilabimus} os nossos inimigos: * e no vosso nome desprezaremos os que se levantam contra nós.
verses.43:7: Pois não esperarei no meu arco: * e a minha espada não me salvará.
verses.43:8: Pois vós nos salvastes dos que nos afligem: * e envergonhastes os que nos odeiam.
verses.43:9: Em Deus seremos louvados o dia todo: * e no vosso nome daremos graças para sempre.
verses.43:10: Mas agora nos repelistes e nos envergonhastes: * e não saireis, Deus, com {virtutibus}.
verses.43:11: Fizestes-nos voltar para trás {post} nossos inimigos: * e os que nos odeiam saqueavam para si.
verses.43:12: {dedisti} como ovelhas {escarum}: * e nos dispersastes entre as nações.
verses.43:13: Vendestes o vosso povo sem preço: * e não houve {multitudo} nas trocas deles.
verses.43:14: Fizestes de nós uma afronta para os nossos vizinhos, * zombaria e {derisum} para os que estão ao nosso redor.
verses.43:15: Fizestes de nós {similitudinem} para as nações: * {commotionem} entre os povos.
verses.43:16: O dia todo a minha {verecundia} está diante de mim, * e a vergonha da minha face me cobriu,
verses.43:17: à voz do que me afronta e {obloquentis}: * diante do inimigo e do que me persegue.
verses.43:18: Tudo isto veio sobre nós, e não vos esquecemos: * e não agimos iniquamente na vossa aliança.
verses.43:19: E o nosso coração {recessit}: * e {declinasti} as nossas veredas do vosso caminho:
verses.43:20: porque nos humilhastes no lugar da aflição, * e a sombra da morte nos cobriu.
verses.43:21: Se esquecemos o nome do nosso Deus, * e se estendemos as nossas mãos para um deus estranho:
verses.43:22: Não pedirá Deus contas disto? * pois ele conhece {abscondita} do coração.
verses.43:22b: Porque por vossa causa somos {mortificamur} o dia todo: * fomos tidos como ovelhas de matança.
verses.43:23: Levantai-vos, por que adormeceis, Senhor? * levantai-vos, e não nos repilais para sempre.
verses.43:24: Por que desviais a vossa face, * esqueceis a nossa carência e a nossa tribulação?
verses.43:25: Pois a nossa alma está humilhada no pó: * o nosso ventre está {conglutinatus} à terra.
verses.43:26: Levantai-vos, Senhor, auxiliai-nos: * e resgatai-nos por causa do vosso nome.

decisions.why: The Latin echoes noun and verb of one root (ἔργον ὃ εἰργάσω, the same echo in the Greek). *operar* keeps it and is current in Brazilian Catholic speech of God's deeds (*Deus operou maravilhas*); *fizestes* (MS1932 *fizeste*, DRB 'wrought') loses the echo. The row *operári iniquitátem → praticar* is for evil-doing and is not touched.

illuminátio → *luz* is the row (26:1 *O Senhor é a minha luz*, φωτισμός both there and here). The row itself notes that 43:4 might keep it apart from 4:7 *lumen vultus tui* (φῶς) → *a luz do vosso rosto* with *iluminação*; but *a iluminação do vosso rosto* is heard as lighting, and it would split illuminátio between 26:1 and here. So one row followed, and 4:7 and 43:4b now read alike in Portuguese where the Latin has two nouns (cost noted).

options.label: a luz
options.note: Ruling: the row (26:1); DRB 'the light', MS1932 *a luz*.

options.label: a iluminação
options.note: the cognate, kept apart from lumen (4:7); heard as lighting.

decisions.why: complacére in (εὐδοκέω ἐν) → *achar prazer em*, the build ruled at 25:3 *complácui in veritáte tua* → *achei prazer na vossa verdade*, where *me comprazi* was bookish to the stylist and unknown to the blind reader. MS1932 *te comprazeste neles*.

options.label: vos agradastes
options.note: DRB 'thou wast pleased with'; *agradar* is complacére's other row (18:15a), with another build.

decisions.latin: Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus
decisions.why: *ipse* stresses the subject (σὺ εἶ αὐτός; DRB 'Thou art thyself'; MS1932 *Tu mesmo és*). *Vós mesmo* keeps it; the adjective is singular because one person is addressed with *vós* (as *vós sois bom*). *Rex meus et Deus meus* is a formula (5:3 *meu Rei e meu Deus*, vocative, no article) and here stands as predicate; kept identical. The one liturgical use found (the Redeemer's feast, aliquibus locis) quotes it with *qui mandas salútes in Jacob*.

options.label: Sois vós
options.note: the stress by order instead of a word.

decisions.why: mandáre with a thing as object → *ordenar* (row: *mandar* alone is heard 'send', 118:138; 32:9 *ele ordenou*). salútes is plural in the Latin and the Greek (τὰς σωτηρίας), the deliverances of Jacob: D6's *salvação* in the plural, which Portuguese can say (unlike *sangues*, D29). MS1932 has the singular. Jacob → *Jacó* (13:7, 19:2).

options.label: ordenais as salvações de Jacó
options.note: Ruling: the row's verb, the Latin's number.

options.label: mandais as salvações de Jacó
options.note: the cognate (41:9 *mandou a sua misericórdia*); heard 'send'.

decisions.why: ventiláre is 'to toss in the air, to winnow' (L&S); with *cornu* the image is a horned beast tossing its enemy (κερατιοῦμεν, 'we will butt'). *lançar ao ar* keeps the Latin's tossing; *derrubar* (DRB 'push down') is the Greek's butting without the air; *sacudir* keeps the toss, not the height. cornu → *chifre* (row). The colon is +3 syllables on the Latin. **v2:** the stylist (worst line) found *com o chifre* trailing after the object; the instrument moved forward (order yields, D2), and the colon ends on *inimigos*.

options.label: derrubaremos
options.note: DRB 'push down'; the Greek's butting; *derrubar* is supplantáre's (17:40).

decisions.why: virtus → *poder* (row, open), and *Dóminus virtútum* → *o Senhor dos poderes* (23:10): the plural of δύναμις is the hosts. *exércitos* (DRB 'armies', MS1932) says the sense but is not the Latin's word — L&S gives no 'troops' for virtus; the sense comes from the Greek — and would break the row the twins will follow (59:12, 107:12 have the same colon, grep). *forças* is fortitúdo's word (17:2). Ruled for the row, as a test for the blind reader: if *os nossos poderes* is heard as 'our abilities', *exércitos* is the honest retreat for all three verses. **v2:** the test failed — the blind reader heard *poderes* as abstract, and the Latinist and the stylist both asked *forças* independently. Taken: the plural *forças* carries strength and armed forces at once, as the Latin plural does, without deciding for *exércitos*. Cost: *fortitúdo → força* (17:2) is the singular of the same word; the singular *virtus* (→ *poder*) and *Dóminus virtútum* (→ *Senhor dos poderes*) are untouched. 59:12b and 107:12b should copy *com as nossas forças*.

options.label: as nossas forças
options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latinist and the stylist; *forças* is both strength and troops in Portuguese, as virtútes is.

options.label: os nossos exércitos
options.note: DRB, MS1932 (*à frente dos nossos exércitos*): the sense, not the word.

decisions.latin: Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros
decisions.why: avértere retrórsum → *voltar para trás* (row: one phrase under either verb, 34:4b), here causative: *Fizestes-nos voltar*. *post* is 'behind, after'; the Greek has παρά ('before, beside'). *atrás dos* beside *para trás* stacks two 'backs' and reads as following the enemy; *diante dos* gives the scene both the Latin and the Greek describe — a rout before the enemy (DRB 'turn our back to our enemies'). **v2:** the Latinist (minor) held *diante* to be the Greek bent against the Latin preposition (rule 1: the Latin governs). His *atrás dos* stacks *para trás, atrás*; *após* is the exact word for *post* and does not repeat *trás*.

options.label: após os
options.note: Ruling (v2): the Latinist; *post* is *após*, and the Latin's openness (behind them, after them) is kept.

options.label: atrás dos
options.note: the Latinist's fix; *para trás, atrás* stacks.

decisions.why: *dare* of persons is 'give up' (DRB 'given us up'); *Destes-nos* at the head of the verse is heard first as 'you gave us (something)'. *entregar* is tráder's verb (26:12), but the two do not meet here, and it is the plainer faithful word. *oves escárum*, 'sheep of foods' (πρόβατα βρώσεως), sheep meant to be eaten: *para comida* keeps the food without naming the slaughterhouse, which is 43:22b's *occisiónis* (MS1932 puts *matadouro* in both).

options.label: Destes-nos … para comida
options.note: the Latin's verb; heard 'gave us' first.

decisions.latin: et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum
decisions.why: multitúdo → *multidão* (row, 5:7b, 30:20). The Latin is open: no great sum was had in their sale (DRB 'no reckoning'), or no crowd of buyers (MS1932 *não houve concorrência no seu mercado*). *multidão* keeps both; *abundância* is abundántia's word and closes the reading to money. commutátio → *troca*.

options.label: multidão
options.note: Ruling: the row; the ambiguity kept.

decisions.why: D39 left this to Ps 43: must *derísum* stay apart from *illúsio → escárnio*? Ruled: **yes**. 78:4 is this verse's near-twin (*oppróbrium vicínis nostris: subsannátio et illúsio his, qui in circúitu nostro sunt*) and varies exactly this one word — and so does the Greek (43:14 καταγέλωτα, 78:4 χλευασμός; read in the Rahlfs text). D15's test keeps a variation the Greek also makes. *riso* is the Latin's own root (*de-rídeo*; *irridére → rir de*, 2:4, 24:3) and the Greek's (κατα-γέλως, laughter-at), and after *afronta* and *zombaria* it is heard as being laughed at. subsannátio → *zombaria* (34:16). Cost: *escarnecer* (derídere, 21:8) and *riso* are not one family in Portuguese.

options.label: riso
options.note: Ruling: kept apart from illúsio (D39), the root of rídeo and γέλως.

options.label: escárnio
options.note: the noun of derídere → escarnecer (21:8); merges 43:14 with 78:4 where the Latin and Greek differ.

options.label: irrisão
options.note: exact, of the same root; likely unknown to the ear.

options.label: chacota
options.note: the Brazilian word for a laughing-stock; colloquial.

decisions.why: similitúdo here is παραβολή: a comparison, what people liken things to — a byword. *comparação* is a sense of the Latin word (L&S 'comparison, simile'); *semelhança* (the cognate, 57:5, 105:20 'likeness') makes no sentence here; *parábola* names the Greek; *fábula* (MS1932) is a story. *Posuísti nos* opens 43:14 and 43:15 alike and is *Fizestes de nós* both times (the pónere + predicate row), so the anaphora stays. **v2:** the stylist found *fazer de nós uma comparação* unidiomatic; *termo de comparação* is the Portuguese phrase and keeps the Latin noun. The ambiguity reader heard it as an example, not a byword — the mocking is carried by 43:15b.

options.label: um termo de comparação
options.note: Ruling (v2): the stylist; the idiom for what things are compared to.

options.label: uma parábola
options.note: the Greek's word; known from the Gospels.

decisions.why: The shaking of the head in scorn (κίνησιν κεφαλῆς). commovére is *abalar* in the psalter (15:8, 20:8), which cannot take a head; 21:8 *movérunt caput → moveram a cabeça* is another verb. *meneio de cabeça* is the Portuguese noun for the gesture; *balançar de cabeça* is plainer but is also a nod. **v2:** the blind reader listed *meneio* as unknown and heard the gesture unclearly; *abanar a cabeça* is the everyday phrase for the sideways shake, not a nod.

options.label: um abanar de cabeça
options.note: Ruling (v2): *abanar a cabeça* is the Brazilian gesture of shaking the head; *meneio* was unknown to the blind reader.

decisions.latin: verecúndia mea … et confúsio faciéi meæ
decisions.why: Two nouns of shame in one verse: *confúsio* → *vergonha* (34:26b, 39:16, settled D41), so *verecúndia* needs another. The Greek pair is ἐντροπή … αἰσχύνη, the same pair as 34:26b *confusióne et reveréntia* (αἰσχύνην καὶ ἐντροπήν) → *vergonha e desonra*: ἐντροπή is *desonra* there, so it is *desonra* here. *contra me* is κατεναντίον μου, 'facing me': *diante de mim* (DRB 'before me'); *contra mim* is heard as 'against me'.

exprobráre → *afrontar* (row; 41:11 *afrontaram-me*). obloqui, 'to speak against, rail at' (L&S, which cites this verse as 'blame, condemn'; παραλαλέω). Once in the psalter (grep). *insultar* is the plain word and free; *difamar* is detráhere's (D41), *censura* vituperátio's (30:13). The object *me* is supplied for both participles (Portuguese *afrontar* wants one; MS1932 *do que me afronta e vitupera*); one article for both, as DRB 'of him that reproacheth and detracteth me' — the Latin does not say whether they are one man or two. **v2:** the Latinist (minor) found the two participles fused into one person while 43:17b keeps two; the article is now repeated (*do que me afronta e do que me insulta*), parallel to *do inimigo e do que me persegue*. His other point, dropping the supplied *me* in all four, is held: *afrontar* and *perseguir* want an object in Portuguese and the psalm is in the first person (grammar, D2); *do que persegue* hangs.

options.label: fala contra mim
options.note: the root of ob-loqui and of the Greek; longer.

decisions.latin: Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum
decisions.why: recédere → *retirar-se* (9:22 *vos retirastes para longe*); *retro* → *para trás*. *voltou atrás* is the idiom, but *voltar para trás* is the avértere / convértere retrórsum phrase (row) and this is another verb (ἀπέστη).

options.label: não voltou atrás
options.note: the idiom (MS1932 *não tornou atrás*); the retrórsum phrase's verb.

decisions.latin: et declinásti sémitas nostras a via tua
decisions.why: The Latin says it positively, as the Greek does (καὶ ἐξέκλινας): 'and you turned our paths aside from your way'. DRB ('neither hast thou') and MS1932 (*nem tu desviaste*) carry the negative of the first colon over — the Hebrew's sense. Rule 1: the Latin as it stands; the hard statement is kept, and the next verse (*porque nos humilhastes*) follows from it. declináre transitive → *apartar* (the verb of declináre a → *apartar-se*, row); *desviar* is avértere's. sémita → *vereda* (D15).

options.label: não apartastes
options.note: DRB, MS1932: the negative carried over; not in the Latin.

decisions.why: The row *abscóndita* (God's, 16:14b) is *coisas escondidas* and names 43:22 as wanting *segredos* for the heart's. *os segredos do coração* is the plainer faithful word (DRB 'the secrets', MS1932 *os segredos*); the root of *esconder* is lost.

decisions.latin: Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die
decisions.why: mortificáre → *dar a morte* (row, 36:32; *mortificar* is ascetic self-denial). The passive is *somos entregues à morte* (MS1932 *somos entregues à morte*). The verse is Rom 8:36 word for word in the Clementine (*Quia propter te mortificamur tota die: aestimati sumus sicut oves occisionis*, fetched to consult/bolls-VULG-45-8.json) and must read alone. *somos mortos* is shorter and exact (DRB 'we are killed') but is heard first as 'we are dead'. *propter te* → *por vossa causa*; commas break the stutter *Porque por*. **v2:** the stylist asked the first colon in one breath; the commas are dropped (*Porque por vossa causa*). æstimári → *ter por*: *fomos tidos como* (stylist; *considerados* was bureaucratic to him), and *ovelhas de matança* keeps the Latin genitive (*oves occisiónis*).

decisions.latin: conglutinátus est in terra venter noster
decisions.why: conglutináre ('glue fast', once in the psalter) is ἐκολλήθη — the Greek verb of adhærére at 21:16 *a minha língua se colou*, where the adhærére row gave *colar-se* for a body part sticking. One Greek, one Portuguese: *colado*. The Latin's *in terra* is where it sticks; Portuguese says *colado à terra*. venter → *ventre* (row). The Sexagesima Introit verse quotes it with *adhǽsit* (missa Quadp2-0) — the same Portuguese serves.

choices.43:2: The vocative *Deus* without *ó* (the Latin has none). áuribus … audívimus kept as the Latin has it (*com os nossos ouvidos ouvimos*). annuntiáre → *anunciar* (D41); its object is 43:2b, so the verse ends on a colon. Used alone as the Sexagesima Introit verse and at Candlemas (missa Quadp2-0, Sancti/02-02); it reads alone.
choices.43:2b: Opus is the object of 43:2's *anunciaram*; DO starts it with a capital after a full stop, Portuguese needs it joined (lower case after 43:2's colon). *in diébus eórum* → *nos dias deles* (*seus* is ambiguous beside *vós*).
choices.43:3: dispérdere → *exterminar* (row), afflígere → *afligir* (row), expéllere → *expulsar* (row, 43:3 named). *plantásti eos* keeps the image (MS1932 *estabeleceste … em seu lugar* explains); *eos* is the fathers, unnamed as in the Latin. v2: *e vós os plantastes* (stylist) marks the change of subject from *a vossa mão*; the ambiguity reader had heard the nations planted. The rhyme *plantastes … expulsastes* is the Latin's parallel (plantásti … expulísti); held.
choices.43:4: *enim* → *pois* (row). *in gládio suo … brácchium eórum*: the Latin's own change of pronoun kept (*suo* reflexive → *a própria espada* in v2, the stylist: *sua* could be heard as God's; then *o braço deles*). possidére → *possuir* (MS1932's *conquistaram* is the Hebrew's sense). *et … non* kept as *e … não*.
choices.43:6: *In te … in nómine tuo* → *Em vós … no vosso nome*, the Latin's preposition kept both times (DRB *Through thee*). spérnere → *desprezar*, insúrgere in → *levantar-se contra* (rows; 43:6 named).
choices.43:8: The subject *vós* supplied after 43:7's first person. confúndere (active) → *envergonhar* (D15; 13:6 *vós envergonhastes*). *affligéntibus* present, as *os que me atribulam*.
choices.43:9: laudári → *ser louvado* (row, 33:3: the Latin's passive; MS1932 *nos gloriaremos* is the Hebrew's). tota die → *o dia todo* (D24). confitéri → *dar graças* (D5); in sǽculum → *para sempre* (D23). The Alleluia verse of Pent23 (missa) has *in sǽcula*; the psalm keeps its own.
choices.43:10: *Nunc autem* → *Mas agora*. repéllere (without *a*) → *repelir* (row, 42:2; 43:10 named). egrediéris is a future → *saireis*. The same colon is 59:12 and 107:12 (*exíbis*): they should copy it (*com as nossas forças*, v2).
choices.43:11: *odérunt* has present sense (24:19 *me odeiam*); *diripiébant* imperfect → *saqueavam* (new row diripere).
choices.43:14: pónere + predicate → *fazer de* (row, 17:12). oppróbrium → *afronta* (row; 30:12 *tornei-me uma afronta … para os meus vizinhos*). in circúitu → *ao redor* (row); *nostro* → *ao nosso redor*.
choices.43:15: géntibus → *para as nações* (dative, as 43:14 *vicínis*); *in pópulis* → *entre os povos*.
choices.43:16: fácies → *face* (vultus is *rosto*). coopéríre → *cobrir*, the same verb as 43:20, kept one. The verse runs on into 43:17 (the cause of the shame), so it ends on a comma.
choices.43:17: *a fácie* of a cause → *diante de* (row, 37:4), so *a fácie inimíci* → *diante do inimigo*. *a voce* → *à voz de* (MS1932). pérsequi → *perseguir*.
choices.43:18: *Hæc ómnia* → *Tudo isto*. *nec* → *e não*, as the Latin (MS1932 *e, ainda assim*, explains). *iníque ágere* → *agir iniquamente* (118:86 *iniquamente*). testaméntum → *aliança* (row; 43:18 named); *in* kept as *na*.
choices.43:20: humiliáre → *humilhar* (row). afflíctio → *aflição*. *umbra mortis* → *a sombra da morte*.
choices.43:22: requírere (God, of sin) → *pedir contas* (row; 9:34 *Não pedirá contas*). *Nonne* is a question that expects yes; *Não pedirá Deus…?* does that. *ista* → *disto*. novit → *conhece* (row).
choices.43:22b: æstimári → *ser tido* (v2, the stylist; draft 1 *considerados*, MS1932). occísio → *matança*; *ovelhas de matança* keeps the genitive (v2; draft 1 *para a matança*). Rom 8:36 = this verse (see `mortificamur`).
choices.43:23: Exsúrge → *Levantai-vos* (row), twice as the Latin. obdormíre → *adormecer* (row, which names 43:23). *ne repéllas* has no object in the Latin; *repelir* needs one, so *nos* is supplied (DRB 'cast us not off'). in finem → *para sempre* (D27, perpetuity). The Sexagesima Introit (missa Quadp2-0) is 43:23–24 and 25b.
choices.43:24: avértere fáciem → *desviar a face* (row, 12:1). *oblivísceris* is a present (the accent; the oblivísci row names 43:24) → *esqueceis*. The Latin has no *et* before it; the asyndeton is kept. inópia → *carência*, of the family of D38's *carente* (inops); tribulátio → *tribulação* (row).
choices.43:25: *humiliáta est … conglutinátus est* as states (*está humilhada … está colado*). *in púlvere* → *no pó*. v2: *Quóniam* → *Pois* (draft 1 *Porque*), which the ambiguity reader heard as *por que* after the two questions of 43:23–24 — the same mend as Ps 42:2.
choices.43:26: adjuváre → *auxiliar* (row), redímere → *resgatar* (row; *resgatai-nos* safe). *propter nomen tuum* → *por causa do vosso nome* (24:11, 30:4). The Litany and Candlemas antiphon (*Exsúrge, Dómine, ádjuva nos, et líbera nos propter nomen tuum*) has another verb in its second half; the psalm keeps its own.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm43.txt, 28 prayed verses (43:2–43:26 with 2b, 4b, 22b; no titulus, D7). One mediant per verse, no flex. Uses (ps032/uses.py): 43:2 Introit verse at Sexagesima and Candlemas; 43:23–26 the Sexagesima Introit; 43:26 the Rogation/Candlemas antiphon (with *líbera*); 43:9 the Pent23 Alleluia (with *in sǽcula*); 43:22b = Rom 8:36 (Clementine fetched, word for word). 43:14 is the near-twin of 78:4; 43:10b the twin of 59:12b and 107:12b.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps043.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932; no DM1962 — not a day-hour psalm). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings applied: D5, D15 (confúndere), D23, D24, D27 (in finem), D36, D38 (inópia → carência, of *carente*), D41 (annuntiáre, confúsio → vergonha). Rows applied: dispérdere, afflígere, expéllere, déxtera, illuminátio, complacére in (25:3), Rex meus et Deus meus, mandáre (thing object → ordenar), cornu, spérnere, insúrgere, laudári, repéllere, retrórsum, dispérgere, multitúdo, pónere + predicate, oppróbrium, subsannátio (34:16), in circúitu, a fácie (37:4), testaméntum, sémita, humiliáre, aliénus, requírere, abscóndita, mortificáre, exsúrgere, obdormíre, avértere fáciem, oblivísci, adjuváre, redímere. D39's open question ruled: derísum → *riso*, apart from illúsio → escárnio (decision `derisum`). Latin kept against DRB/MS1932: 43:19 *apartastes* positive; 43:9 passive *seremos louvados*; 43:5 plural *salvações*.

Draft 1: hard pass (after fixing a doubled article at 43:11 *diante dos os*). Length: +5 at 43:6a (*lançaremos ao ar* for ventilábimus, see `ventilabimus`), 43:19a (*não se retirou para trás*, four Latin words), 43:22b first colon (*entregues à morte* for one verb; Rom 8:36 must read alone); +4 at 43:11a, 43:12a, 43:14a; −7 at 43:13b (commutatiónibus is one long word); −4 at 43:10b; ±3 elsewhere — accepted, each the Latin's content. Rhyme 43:3 *plantastes … expulsastes*: the Latin's own parallel (plantásti … expulísti), the vós preterite; kept. Oxytone finals where the Latin is paroxytone (43:4b, 43:5, 43:14b, 43:20a, 43:24b, 43:25a …): *nós*, *Jacó*, *redor*, *aflição*, *tribulação*, *pó* — the Latin's words at the cadence; allowed by rule 4.
